title: Cross-stitch cat in a window silhouette
subtitle: A single-colour silhouette design on 14-count white Aida
excerpt: A cat sitting upright in a window frame, stitched as a simple silhouette in one colour on 14-count white Aida. The design is approximately 70 by 90 stitches and finishes at around 12 by 16 cm. The back-stitch window frame and the solid fill contrast against the white fabric background.
sourceNotes: Original silhouette design. Single-colour silhouette stitching is a classic beginner pattern format in British cross-stitch publishing.

glossaryTerms.definition: A woven fabric designed for cross-stitch, made from cotton threads grouped into regular blocks with a visible hole at each corner. The number of blocks per inch is the count; 14-count Aida has 14 stitching squares per inch.

content.text: This single-colour silhouette suits a first full project. All the stitching is standard

Find the head section on the chart and stitch the ear tips first, then fill downward through the head, body and tail in rows. Silhouette designs stitch faster than multi-colour designs because there is no colour-changing.
Fill the complete silhouette with cross-stitch.
Work in horizontal rows where possible. The window sill below the cat and the window frame outline are both filled solid in the same colour. Leave the window pane area within the frame empty.
Add the window frame in back-stitch.
Work the window frame edges and the central cross-bar of the window in back-stitch using two strands. The back-stitch lines sit directly on the filled Aida squares at the frame edge.
Trim to a 5 cm border and mount in a 15 × 20 cm frame. The white Aida background provides all the negative space the design needs; no additional background stitching is required.
